title: Homemade Golden Syrup
description: Simple homemade golden syrup for dumplings, baking and pancakes. Choose white sugar, a white/yellow cane sugar blend, or all yellow cane sugar.

options.label: white sugar
options.note: Closest to classic golden syrup; caramelise the first 100 g until deep amber.

options.label: half white, half yellow cane sugar
options.note: Darker and more caramel-like; use white sugar for the first caramel.

options.label: yellow cane sugar (đường mía)
options.note: Strongest cane/molasses flavour. Colour is dark from the start, so take care not to burn the caramel.

steps.text: Put the first 100 g sugar and 30 mL water in a heavy saucepan. Heat over medium heat until amber; swirl instead of stirring. With yellow cane sugar, colour is harder to judge, so avoid burning it.
Carefully add the remaining 400 g sugar and 270 mL water. It may bubble, splutter and briefly harden. Stir gently until any hard caramel dissolves.
Add lemon juice and, if using, the peel. Simmer uncovered on very low heat for 40–55 minutes, without stirring, until syrupy. It gets much thicker as it cools; avoid reducing it to a hard caramel.

Remove the lemon peel. Let the syrup cool, then transfer to a clean dry jar. If too thick once cool, loosen gently with a little hot water. Store sealed, use a clean spoon, and discard if mould develops.

notes: Yield is an estimate based on around 640 g of finished syrup. Actual volume and nutrition per 100 g depend on how far the water cooks off; expect roughly 450–500 mL of pourable syrup.
Yellow cane sugar changes flavour and colour far more than calorie content. Nutrition is estimated for all sugar options using typical sugar values.
Hot caramel and syrup can cause serious burns; add water carefully.
